title: Subcutaneous amyloidoma models for screening potential anti-fibrillating agents in vivo
protocol: Dissolve insulin in citrate phosphate buffer (pH-2.6) for solubility.
Locate a spot and insert the needle subcutaneously.
Gently and slowly inject insulin (fibrillated) and insulin with IS1 (non-fibrillated) on the contralateral sides of the vertebrae.
Repeat the injection once daily for 28 consecutive days at the same injection site.
Dilute insulin in PBS (pH-7.4) before administration to mice.
Administer diluted insulin subcutaneously at the same site for better amyloid formation.
Monitor mice post-insulin administration for signs of hypoglycemic shock.
Prick mouse tail with a needle to obtain blood and check blood glucose level using a glucometer.
Inject 100 μl of 20% glucose intraperitoneally in case of hypoglycemia detected.
Check whether the blood glucose level has recovered to a normoglycemic state after glucose injection.
Excise the amyloidoma along with the surrounding tissue carefully using scissors.
Weigh the mass of the excised skin biopsy and record it.
Store the excised tissue in 10% formalin.
Immerse the tissue in paraffin at 58°C.
Cut the tissues into sections 10 μm thick using a rotary microtome.
Dry heat the slides at 85°C for 15–20 min to dissolve wax.
Immerse the slides in Coplin jars containing xylene for 2 min, repeat two more times at room temperature.
Serially immerse the slides in a gradient of alcohol according to a specified protocol.
Dip the slides in tap water for about 2 min.
Float the sections in a 56°C water bath.
Mount the sections onto slides and dry them overnight at room temperature.
Immerse the slides in a Coplin jar containing Congo Red Solution.
Incubate the slides for 15–20 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse the slides in distilled water.
Dip the slides in alkaline alcohol solution (5–10 dips).
Rinse the slides in tap water.
Immerse the slides in a Coplin jar containing 90% alcohol for 3 minutes.
Immerse the slides in two changes of 100% alcohol for 3 minutes each at room temperature.
Immerse the slides in two changes of xylene for 3 minutes each at room temperature.
Mount the slides with DPX.
Observe the slides with a polarized light microscope.
